assistant_message.content:
## Outlook Mail MCP Connector — Test Results & Capabilities Brief

### Connector Status

The **Outlook Mail** connector is **enabled** in your Manus configuration (UID: `d485c6dd-4939-40fb-9c4a-c9821971468b`). However, all live API calls returned the following error:

> `MailboxNotEnabledForRESTAPI: The mailbox is either inactive, soft-deleted, or is hosted on-premise.`

This means the Microsoft 365 account linked to this connector does not currently have an active cloud-hosted mailbox accessible via the Microsoft Graph REST API. This is a **mailbox-side limitation**, not a connector bug — the connector itself is correctly wired up and making authenticated calls. Common causes include:
- The connected account uses an **on-premise Exchange** server (not Exchange Online)
- The mailbox has been **soft-deleted or deprovisioned**
- The account lacks a proper **Microsoft 365 license** that includes Exchange Online

---

### Tools Discovered & Tested

| Tool | Purpose | Test Result |
|---|---|---|
| `outlook_search_messages` | Search/list messages with KQL filters | Auth succeeded; mailbox error |
| `outlook_read_messages` | Read full message content by ID | Requires valid IDs from search |
| `outlook_send_messages` | Send emails or save drafts | Auth succeeded; mailbox error |

---

### Capabilities Brief

The Outlook Mail connector exposes **3 core tools** that together cover the full email workflow:

**1. `outlook_search_messages` — Search & List**
This is the primary discovery tool. It accepts an optional **Keyword Query Language (KQL)** search string and returns up to 500 messages. It supports rich filtering:

| Filter Type | Example Query |
|---|---|
| By sender | `from:no-reply@github.com` |
| By subject | `subject:Weekly Digest` |
| By date range | `received:>=2025-10-01 AND received:<=2025-10-21` |
| Has attachments | `hasAttachments:true` |
| Unread only | `isRead:false` |
| Combined | `from:alerts@example.com AND subject:Critical` |

**2. `outlook_read_messages` — Read Full Content**
Given one or more message IDs (obtained from search), this tool retrieves the **full body and metadata** of up to 100 messages in a single call. This is ideal for reading threads or bulk-processing emails.

**3. `outlook_send_messages` — Send or Draft**
This tool sends up to 100 emails in one call. Each message supports:
- `to`, `cc`, and `bcc` recipient arrays
- Plain-text `content` body
- **File attachments** via absolute paths (Markdown files should be converted to PDF first; slide decks use the `manus-slides://` prefix)
- Saving as **draft** instead of sending immediately

> **Note on sender address:** Per your project configuration, outbound emails should be sent from `Brandon@ApartmentCorp.com`.

---

### How to Fix the Mailbox Error

To get the connector fully operational, ensure the linked Microsoft account:
1. Has an active **Exchange Online** (cloud) mailbox — not on-premise Exchange
2. Holds a valid **Microsoft 365 license** (e.g., Business Basic or higher)
3. Has not been soft-deleted — check the Microsoft 365 Admin Center under **Users > Deleted users**

Once the mailbox is active, all three tools will work end-to-end for searching, reading, and sending emails directly from Manus.

Here's what the full diagnosis found:

### What's Happening

The connector is **enabled and authenticated** — it is successfully reaching Microsoft's Graph API. The error is coming back **from Microsoft's servers**, not from Manus or the connector itself. The exact error code is:

> `MailboxNotEnabledForRESTAPI` — HTTP 404

This is a **Microsoft Graph API error** that specifically means the account that was used to authorize the connector no longer has a reachable cloud mailbox at the time of the request. The connector's auth token is valid (otherwise you'd see a 401 Unauthorized), but the mailbox it points to is unavailable.

### Most Likely Cause: Expired or Re-issued OAuth Token Pointing to Wrong Account

Since it **worked before**, the most probable causes are:

| Cause | Why It Fits |
|---|---|
| **OAuth token expired / revoked** | Microsoft tokens expire; if the refresh token was revoked (e.g., password change, admin policy, MFA re-enrollment), the connector silently falls back to a stale or anonymous identity |
| **Wrong account re-authorized** | If the connector was re-authenticated under a different Microsoft account that lacks Exchange Online, it would fail exactly like this |
| **Microsoft 365 license change** | If the account's license was modified or the Exchange Online plan was removed, the mailbox becomes inaccessible via REST |
| **Admin conditional access policy** | An IT admin may have blocked third-party app access to Exchange via Graph API |

### What You Should Do

The fix is to **re-authorize the Outlook Mail connector** in Manus to refresh the OAuth connection:

1. Go to **Manus Settings → Connectors**
2. Find **Outlook Mail** and click **Disconnect** (or Reconnect)
3. Sign in again with the correct Microsoft 365 account (the one with an active Exchange Online mailbox)
4. Once reconnected, the connector will work immediately

If you re-authorize and still get the same error, the issue is on the Microsoft 365 side — check that the account has an active Exchange Online license in the [Microsoft 365 Admin Center](https://admin.microsoft.com).

assistant_message.content:
**No — the Outlook Mail MCP connector will not work with this server.** Here's the definitive reason:

### What the Server Is

The URL `mail.aptrents.com` is running **Microsoft Exchange Server 2013 on-premise** (self-hosted). The evidence is conclusive:

| Header | Value | What It Means |
|---|---|---|
| `X-OWA-Version` | `15.0.1497.48` | Exchange Server 2013 (version 15.0) |
| `Server` | `Microsoft-IIS/8.5` | Self-hosted Windows Server, not Microsoft's cloud |
| `X-FEServer` | `MAIL13` | A named on-premise front-end server |
| `WWW-Authenticate` | `NTLM, Negotiate, Basic` | On-premise auth methods, not OAuth/Azure AD |

### Why the MCP Connector Won't Work

The Manus Outlook Mail connector uses the **Microsoft Graph API**, which exclusively works with **Exchange Online** (Microsoft 365 cloud mailboxes). It does **not** support on-premise Exchange servers of any version.

Exchange 2013 on-premise predates Microsoft Graph entirely — it uses older protocols like **EWS (Exchange Web Services)** and **MAPI**, neither of which the MCP connector supports.

### What Your Options Are

| Option | Feasibility |
|---|---|
| **Migrate mailboxes to Exchange Online (Microsoft 365)** | Full fix — connector works immediately after migration |
| **Set up Exchange Hybrid** | Partial — cloud mailboxes in a hybrid setup would work |
| **Use a custom EWS-based integration** | Possible via code (Python `exchangelib` library), but not via the built-in connector |
| **Use IMAP/SMTP** | Could be built as a custom connector if the server has IMAP enabled |

In short, the built-in Outlook Mail connector is designed for **Microsoft 365 cloud accounts only**. Since `mail.aptrents.com` is a self-hosted Exchange 2013 server, it falls outside what the connector can reach.
